./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:5:Turn Versionless from an early migration-toolkit design into a working, extensible, local-first migration spine that proves genuinely old React and Angular applications can be modernized with behavioral parity. Use a varied corpus of real OSS applications to decide how much Node, bundler, and browser-conformance infrastructure is actually necessary. Make enterprise evidence automatic through per-migration audit receipts and a project-level trust package.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:19:Owner update, 2026-08-08: permission from the owner must never block, pause, or terminal-wait the overall goal. Standing authority covers the bounded, non-destructive OSS fixture acquisition and local evidence work already described by this charter. A harness, sandbox, credential, or tool-level approval failure may block only its exact task; the PM must immediately advance other safe goal work and must not repeatedly ask the owner to restate authorization. Environment enforcement still applies and must not be bypassed.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:23:Owner update, 2026-08-08 (production-readiness denominator): the current four-application Witness matrix qualifies the harness only; it cannot establish production readiness. The minimum counted production-readiness corpus is twelve distinct real, permissively licensed legacy applications: at least four React applications, four Angular-lineage applications spanning AngularJS and Angular, and four older Next.js applications, with a target of five per lane when eligible evidence survives the hard gates. Every counted application must have pinned provenance and license evidence, an honest legacy baseline and migrated output, two deterministic real-browser passes per lane through the direct linked Witness implementation, meaningful application-specific interaction and state assertions, mutation sensitivity and restoration, local-first network evidence, and machine/human receipts. Production readiness additionally requires representative Node-upgrade and bundler-era coverage (including webpack and older Vite where eligible), at least one designated real pilot for React and Angular plus a first-class Next.js pilot, and a reproducible aggregate trust package. Report this as a named scoreboard with numerator, denominator, failures, and missing gates; do not repeat an ungrounded readiness percentage.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:25:Production readiness scoreboard, 2026-08-08: React 1/4 (`react-boilerplate-v4-composed`); Angular-lineage 1/4 (`angular-realworld-v15-to-v16`); older Next.js 1/4 (`next-killedbygoogle-derived-state-to-memo`). Harness qualification 0/4. Designated pilots: React 0/1; Angular 0/1; Next.js 0/1. Counted cell gates: pinned MIT provenance pass; direct linked Witness 2+2 passes pass; meaningful behavior/parity pass; mutation/restoration pass; process-local offline evidence pass; machine/human receipt and atomic aggregate linkage pass; fresh unsandboxed full suite 537/537 across 72 files; 14-receipt/27-dependency deterministic trust replay pass with core `abf4dd55764cd886eb28f62b0a08ee308bbd960e72ffc60da5baa056969a2c7d`. Missing: React 3, Angular-lineage 3, Next.js 3, all three pilots, harness qualification, and remaining representative Node/bundler/package-manager coverage.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:33:- Completion proof: A varied, licensed, reproducibly pinned corpus of real legacy React and Angular OSS applications—including at least one designated pilot per framework—migrates through a documented Versionless workflow, builds on supported Node targets, and passes local Playwright behavioral-parity journeys. Each run emits a machine-readable and human-readable audit receipt; the project emits an automatically generated trust package.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:36:- Blind spots considered: Fixture licensing and provenance; framework/Node/bundler coupling; absent baseline verification; browser-test flakiness; accidental network egress; frontend payment-data exposure; supply-chain evidence; generated evidence versus formal certification; premature generic abstraction
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:37:- Existing plan facts: `DESIGN.md` must be inspected and validated in execution. React and Angular come first. Other frameworks need credible extension seams but no first-tranche implementation. The legacy-app dataset must be real, varied, licensed, and reproducible. Conformance investment follows corpus evidence. Node upgrades, webpack, older Vite, Playwright, Vitest/Browser Mode, async/witness, unplugin, and Codemod are explicit evidence targets. Both run-level receipts and a project trust package are required. Versionless-owned code is strict TypeScript and the repository uses the `DESIGN.md` Vite+ pnpm-monorepo stack.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:45:`From clean, pinned OSS inputs, a Judge-approved corpus of at least four real legacy React apps, four Angular-lineage apps, and four older Next.js apps—including designated pilots and representative Node/bundler eras—can be migrated reproducibly through a strict-TypeScript Versionless implementation in a Vite+ pnpm monorepo; supported outputs build and pass two deterministic direct-Witness browser-parity runs per baseline and migrated lane; unexpected manual intervention and network egress are surfaced; each run produces an auditable receipt; and the Versionless repository produces a current aggregate trust package.`
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:47:The coverage policy must be fixed from evidence before corpus implementation so fixture selection cannot be tuned to the tool. The current four-app matrix is a harness-qualification prerequisite, not corpus completion. Count no application until its canonical baseline/migrated two-pass Witness evidence and required receipts are published and verified. At minimum the production corpus must cover four React, four Angular-lineage, and four older Next.js applications; multiple materially different legacy eras; webpack; older Vite where a representative app exists; relevant package-manager and Node constraints; and designated pilots for React, Angular, and Next.js. Target five applications per lane when candidates meet the immutable-provenance, license, meaningful-journey, reproducibility, and locality hard gates. Any excluded or unsupported case must remain visible in the aggregate report with a reason.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:51:Production-readiness updates must use the durable scoreboard: counted/passing applications by lane against the 4/4/4 minimum, harness-qualification status, designated-pilot status, Node/bundler coverage, locality, mutation/restoration, receipts, and trust replay. Percentages are prohibited unless their denominator and every contributing evidence item are shown and have materially changed since the prior update.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:61:After the first vertical slice, use its failures and receipts to size further conformance, Node, bundler, and compliance work. Continue through the remaining corpus and trust-evidence gaps. Do not stop after producing a roadmap, architecture decision, fixture catalog, or one successful application.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:77:- Generate both per-run migration evidence and a project trust package. Reports must be machine-readable, human-readable, reproducible where practical, and honest about unknowns or failures.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:78:- Map evidence to relevant enterprise review concerns such as data flow, access, change history, SBOM, dependency and license inventory, vulnerability state, provenance, and PCI DSS/SOC 2 control questions. Do not claim that generated evidence is certification or legal attestation.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:81:- Treat the initial four-app direct-Witness matrix only as harness qualification. Do not claim production readiness until canonical evidence counts at least four distinct real applications in each of the React, Angular-lineage, and older Next.js lanes, with two deterministic baseline and migrated passes per app plus meaningful parity, mutation/restoration, locality, provenance, and receipt gates.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:82:- Require production evidence beyond app count: designated React, Angular, and Next.js pilots; representative legacy and target Node lanes; webpack and eligible older-Vite paths; documented package-manager/native-build/manual-intervention outcomes; and one reproducible aggregate enterprise trust package. Honest unsupported and failed cases remain in the denominator-facing report.
./docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/goal.md:94:Do not stop after planning, discovery, or Judge selection while a safe Worker task can advance working software. Do not stop after one verified Worker package when corpus, browser-parity, Node/bundler, locality, receipt, or trust-package evidence still has a safe local follow-up.

item.text:
Implemented npm-lock trust hardening:

- Added explicit fail-closed exclusions for `react-dashboard` and `angular-contacts`, bound to the exact T190 evidence digest.
- Trust generation now rejects missing, reordered, altered, or inconsistent exclusion records.
- Provenance embeds those exclusions; verification independently checks them against aggregate evidence.
- Added regression tests for missing exclusions, altered state, digest tampering, and recomputed provenance tampering.
- `git diff --check` and JSON validation pass.

Tests could not run because dependencies are unavailable locally. Both the required `vp` command and an offline install failed due missing cached tarballs (`playwright-core` and `@types/node`). No network access was used.
